name: Intuitive Machines IM-2 (Athena)
short_status: Partial: landed on its side in a crater on Mons Mouton Mar 6, 2025 (southernmost lunar landing); mission ended Mar 7, 2025 after about 13 hours.
tagline: Intuitive Machines · United States · Lander · 2025 · Commercial and multipolar Partial
stats: off target, inside a 20 m shadowed crater

facts.label: CLPS task order
facts.value: About $47 million to deliver PRIME-1, awarded 16 October 2020

facts.label: Launch
facts.value: 26 February 2025, 7:16 p.m. EST (Feb 27, 00:16:30 UTC), Falcon 9 from KSC LC-39A

facts.label: Rideshares
facts.value: NASA Lunar Trailblazer orbiter and AstroForge Odin flew on the same Falcon 9; both were lost after deployment

facts.label: Landing
facts.value: 6 March 2025, 17:28 UTC (about 11:30 a.m. CST), near the center of Mons Mouton

facts.label: Site coordinates
facts.value: 84.7906 S, 29.1957 E, on its side within a 20-meter-diameter crater

facts.label: Southernmost landing
facts.value: Landed closer to the lunar south pole than any previous lander (still the record as of October 2026)

facts.label: Landing error
facts.value: More than 1,300 feet (400 meters) from the intended landing site

facts.label: Mission end
facts.value: Declared over 7 March 2025, 12:15 a.m. CST, about 13 hours after touchdown, after batteries depleted

facts.label: Data returned
facts.value: 250 MB collected for NASA; LROC team cites over 400 MB total sent back

facts.label: PRIME-1 results
facts.value: TRIDENT drill demonstrated full range of motion; MSOLO detected elements likely from the lander's propulsion gases

facts.label: Undeployed payloads
facts.value: Grace hopper, Lunar Outpost MAPP rover (with MIT AstroAnt), Dymon Yaoki rover, and Nokia's 4G surface demo never deployed or completed

facts.label: IM-3 target
facts.value: Targeted for the first part of 2027 to the Reiner Gamma swirl (NASA's Moon Base program manager and Intuitive Machines' chief executive, reported by Aerospace America on 15 September 2026); NASA's launch schedule lists early 2027 (updated 21 October 2026)

facts.label: Sixth CLPS award
facts.value: Announced 30 June 2026: up to $148.3 million for a production-line Nova-C delivery by 2028

timeline: NASA awards Intuitive Machines about $47M to deliver the PRIME-1 drill and spectrometer
Launch at 7:16 p.m. EST on Falcon 9 from KSC LC-39A, with Lunar Trailblazer and Odin ridesharing
Touchdown at 17:28 UTC on Mons Mouton: southernmost lunar landing, but on its side in a crater
Mission declared over at 12:15 a.m. CST; LRO images the lander in its crater at 16:54 UTC
LRO acquires a closer oblique view of Athena at 14:52 UTC
CEO Steve Altemus details the issues that prevented an upright touchdown and fixes for IM-3
IM-3 targeted to the Reiner Gamma swirl (as of Oct 2026; it was on schedule for the second half of 2026 as of Jun 2026)
